overall: Atlanta is warming steadily this morning with a running max of 82.4°F at 11:09 ET and a current warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, though the 30-minute velocity of +3.6°F/hr suggests an accelerating warm-up. Skies are broken overcast (BKN, ceiling ~1,600 ft) which is partially suppressing heating, but southwest flow and high dewpoints (73.4°F) are keeping the atmosphere primed for afternoon convection. The day is broadly tracking toward the upper end of expectations, though cloud cover and a 40% chance of afternoon thunderstorms after 1pm introduce downside risk to the peak.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notable: HRRR (89.0°F) and NWS (near 89°F) are in tight agreement at the warm end, while ECMWF is a sharp outlier at 83.8°F — potentially reflecting earlier or heavier cloud/precip impacts — and NBM splits the difference at 86.0°F. The INTRADAY model is strongly concentrated on 88–89°F (55.6%), and the META (fused) model also peaks there at 26.6%, lending confidence to the upper-80s target, though the ensemble signals show high entropy and flag the situation as difficult to trade.
max_temp_prediction: With ~3 hours remaining until the predicted peak (~14:24 ET), the current 82.4°F base and sustained warming velocity support reaching the upper 80s — a linear extrapolation at the 2-hour velocity (+2.7°F/hr) implies roughly 88–90°F. The primary downside risk is early convective initiation (storms possible after 1pm) cutting off the warming trend, which the ECMWF's cooler 83.8°F may be capturing. Balancing the strong HRRR/NWS/INTRADAY/META consensus near 89°F against the ECMWF outlier and afternoon storm risk, the best estimate is approximately 88.5°F with moderate-to-low confidence given cloud suppression and convective uncertainty.
